authority_move.position: second of Phase 4 S7's seven authority moves
authority_move.why_declaration_only: Unmake's three corrections landed in Phase 0B — the owner handshake, the magic-only damage_classes with all three attack classes, and AURA_ARM — and the pair engine keeps magic_amp because golden pins it. What was still missing is the one thing Phase 4 introduces: HolderStacking.IDEMPOTENT_AURA, the declaration that makes its arm-time dedupe key (subject, mechanic_id) and stops two holders cursing one enemy twice (D-66). This commit gives that declaration its live consumer.

landed_against.rule: R-17/R-32/D-97 — no baseline moves inside this commit

qualifying_population.declared_in: docs/receipts/campaign-fingerprints.json wall.P4-S7, and the S7c1 commit body
qualifying_population.rule: A leaf can move only where two or more roster participants hold one IDEMPOTENT_AURA mechanic, because that is the only condition under which arm_key's aura branch collides. Abyssal Mask is the only mechanic declaring that stacking. Over the committed coupled scenario set, exactly one scenario equips Abyssal Mask at all — mandate_abyssal_curse_roster, on one participant — and the other twelve equip it on none, so the two-holder condition is unreachable in every scenario rather than merely unobserved. The four bench scenarios fix no Abyssal Mask on any loadout and the optimizer proposes items for the main champion only, which is one holder.

golden.why: Unmake is a walk packet; the pair snapshot never composes a roster.

bench.per_scenario: 0 for each of the four scenarios

measured.bench: All four scenarios identical on every counter family, the residual, the rung histogram, the winner and the score (4003.1 / 5010.8 / 3305.0 / 4642.3); row 11 routing_divergences [] x4.
measured.positive_control: tests/test_holder_stacking.py::test_two_abyssal_holders_curse_one_enemy_once_and_say_so runs a roster that really holds Abyssal Mask twice: two Unmake packets are authored, one arms, and the other is published with applied_amount 0 and a dedupe block naming the holder that armed first. So the zeros above are a dedupe that landed and had nothing in the baselines to collide with, not a code path that never runs.
measured.note: The declared count and the measured count agree; nothing qualifies under R-15 and no oracle receipt is owed.

behaviour_the_first_implementation_had_a.what: A first cut keyed the ledger on arm_key alone and dropped any repeat, which collapsed every Carve stack after the first and every Expose Weakness re-arm — 131 coupled-golden leaves, measured, on scenarios cleaver_bloodsong_roster and mandate_abyssal_curse_roster.
behaviour_the_first_implementation_had_a.why_it_was_wrong: A collision is between two *holders*. One holder arming the same (subject, mechanic, holder) key repeatedly is a re-arm — Carve arms once per damage event — and collapsing those answers a question no mechanic declares.
behaviour_the_first_implementation_had_a.how_it_is_now_unrepresentable: ArmingLedger.admit drops only when the recorded first holder differs from the arming holder, so a PER_HOLDER key — which keeps the holder and therefore can never collide across holders — is never dropped at all. Pinned by tests/test_holder_stacking.py::test_one_holder_re_arming_over_time_is_never_a_duplicate, parametrised over all five dual-sided mechanics.
